intro: A cache hit changes recency even though no new key is inserted. Tracing every request makes the difference between insertion order and LRU eviction visible.
task: Trace cache hits and evictions, refreshing recency on every hit before the next admission decision.
requirements: requests is a list or tuple of at most 10000 nonempty string keys; capacity is an integer 0..10000.
On a hit, move that key to most-recently-used position. On a miss with positive capacity, insert it and evict the least-recently-used key if full.
Return dict hits as a boolean vector, keys as the final most-recent-first list, and evicted as keys in eviction order. Capacity zero stores nothing and records no evictions.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: A hit is a state transition
hints.body: Remove a hit from its old position before moving it to the front.

hints.title: Evict from the opposite end
hints.body: The final element of a most-recent-first list is the least recently used.

explanation: LRU approximates temporal locality: recently accessed keys are retained in preference to older ones. A hit must refresh recency or the policy becomes insertion-order eviction.
This list-based implementation makes state transitions transparent and has linear lookup cost. A production cache can combine a dictionary with a linked order structure for constant-time operations.
